title: Usage Buffer Ladders & Prorated Smoothing for Dedicated Capacity — Pilot
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary: Pilot a new pricing construct for Dedicated GPU reservations that reduces abrupt overage churn and improves predictable economics for enterprise customers. The core idea is a two-part mechanism: 1) Usage buffer ladders — tiered ‘soft reserve’ buffers that give customers incremental headroom at progressively higher overage rates, and 2) Prorated smoothing — a time-windowed smoothing algorithm that prorates short spikes across a configurable billing window before applying overage billing. Together these aim to reduce surprise bills, simplify contract language around burst, and preserve revenue capture for sustained overuse.

Why this is different: Existing playbooks focus on fixed burst credits or flat surge pricing. This pilot tests a graduated buffer band (0–10%, 10–25%, 25–50%) with corresponding overage unit multipliers and an adjustable smoothing window (1h, 6h, 24h). The goal is to find a balance where short operational spikes are absorbed without switching customers to higher commitment tiers, while long sustained overuse still monetizes fairly.

Goals & Success Metrics:
- Reduce customer-initiated downgrade churn related to surprise overage by 40% among pilot cohort.
- Decrease mean frequency of support billing disputes for Dedicated customers by 60% within 3 months.
- Maintain or increase revenue per reserved GPU-hour for accounts that exceed reserved baseline >10% month-over-month (target +5%).
- Measure SLO compliance and incident correlation: ensure smoothing window does not materially increase latency or capacity contention (no >1% increase in tail latency incidents).

Pilot design:
- Cohort: 6 enterprise customers across SMB and mid-market who currently use Dedicated and have experienced 10–60% month spikes. Two customers are on existing flex bursts, four have fixed reserves.
- Buckets: Soft buffer tiers at 0–10% (no multiplier), 10–25% (1.5x unit overage), 25–50% (2.5x unit overage).
- Smoothing windows configurable per-customer: default 6h, options 1h or 24h. Billing engine prorates token/GPU-hour consumption across window before assigning to bucket.
- SLA mapping: Larger buffers and shorter smoothing windows are available to higher SLA tiers (SLA-99.9 → +25% buffer, SLA-99.95 → +50% buffer) with contracted pricing for those addons.

Contract & SQ workstream:
- Addendum: Create a ‘Capacity Buffer Addendum’ to enterprise contracts documenting buffer definitions, overage multipliers, smoothing windows, and audit rights. Legal draft link in attachments.
- Security Questionnaire (SQ): Update responses to cover concerns about capacity isolation, billing telemetry, and audit logs (items: capacity tagging, per-request region/instance attribution, KMS-wrapped billing data). SQ owners: Rachel Kim (Security) and Tom Bhatia (Legal).

Implementation trade-offs & risks:
- Complexity vs clarity: Graduated buffers are more accurate but harder to explain. We will create simple customer-facing visuals and an interactive calculator in Console to make economics transparent.
- Billing system changes: Requires batching at 1h/6h/24h windows before billing pass — small performance cost and complexity in historical charge reconciliation. Engineering will maintain raw per-minute metrics for audits.
- Gaming risk: Customers could shift workloads to avoid falling into higher multiplier bands. We will monitor patterning and impose anti-abuse rules (e.g., sustained pattern >72h moves baseline recommendation).

Rollout plan & timeline:
- Week 0–2 (Design): Finalize multipliers, smoothing defaults, and contract language. Links: design doc (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-buffer-design, legal draft: https://drive.google.com/file/d/example-contract-addendum.
- Week 3–5 (Infra): ENG implements smoothing layer and billing integration (feature branch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1580).
- Week 6 (Pilot): Onboard 6 customers; run for 8 weeks. Create weekly dashboard in Console to track metrics (dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/usage-buffer-pilot).
- Week 14 (Review): Analyze outcomes, decide whether to generalize, iterate multipliers, or retire pilot.

Open questions for PM/Eng/Legal:
1) Should we allow per-project vs per-account smoothing windows? (Trade-off: flexibility vs billing complexity)
2) What default multiplier should apply for region-constrained GPUs where capacity is already tight?
3) Do we tie buffer sizes to existing committed tiers or make them orthogonal add-ons?

Artifacts & links: see attachments.

Next steps (owner: Alex Chen):
- Finalize buffer multipliers and smoothing defaults with Eng by 2025-02-20.
- Draft Customer-facing pricing FAQ and Console calculator mockups with Design.
- Kick off legal addendum draft and SQ updates with Security and Legal teams.
